notes: Score commit boundaries and message quality separately. A polished message around an incoherent diff fails. Well-split commits with vague subjects also fail. No run may commit, stage destructively, or discard work.

evals.prompt: I fixed the off-by-one in the pagination offset. Commit it.
evals.expected_output: One commit, subject only, no body.
assertions: It reads the staged or unstaged diff before writing the message
The subject names the behaviour fixed rather than saying fix
No body is added
No issue reference is used as the subject

evals.prompt: Commit the webhook idempotency fix and its regression test.
evals.expected_output: One commit containing both, not two.
assertions: Implementation and test go in the same commit
The reasoning references revertability or coherence rather than a rule about tests
The subject describes the behaviour change, not the files

evals.prompt: I refactored the billing module to extract a service, and while I was in there I fixed the currency rounding bug. Commit.
evals.expected_output: Two commits proposed, refactor first, with approval sought before creating them.
assertions: It proposes splitting into a refactor commit and a behaviour-fix commit
The refactor is ordered first so a reviewer can confirm it changed nothing
It does not create the commits without approval
Each proposed subject would revert as one decision

evals.prompt: I ran the formatter across the repo and also changed the retry limit from 3 to 5. Commit everything.
evals.expected_output: Split, because the formatting would bury the semantic change in blame.
assertions: It proposes separating the formatter run from the retry change
The reason given is that the mechanical change would hide the semantic one in review or blame
It does not cite a line-count threshold as the deciding factor
It stages by path rather than staging everything

evals.prompt: Commit the schema change. I also updated the generated types file.
evals.expected_output: One commit, because source and generated artifact must stay synchronised.
assertions: Source and generated output go in one commit
The reason is that splitting creates a commit where they disagree
It does not propose a separate generated-files commit

evals.expected_output: An inspection of the whole tree first, and a question or a split proposal if it holds unrelated work.
assertions: It runs git status and reads the diffs before staging
It does not run git add . or git add -A
If unrelated changes exist, it asks or proposes a grouping rather than committing a mixture
It reports what it left unstaged

evals.prompt: Commit the auth fix. Note that I have unfinished work in packages/ui that I do not want committed.
evals.expected_output: Only the auth paths staged, the UI work untouched and explicitly acknowledged.
assertions: Only the auth-related paths are staged, by name
The packages/ui changes are neither staged nor modified
It never runs checkout, restore, reset --hard, clean, or stash drop
The response states what was left alone

evals.prompt: config.ts has both my new feature flag and a debug console.log I want to keep locally. Commit just the flag.
evals.expected_output: Hunk-level staging, or a proposal for the user to run it interactively.
assertions: It proposes git add -p or an equivalent hunk-level approach
It does not stage the whole file
It does not delete or revert the debug line
If the hunks are entangled, it asks rather than guessing

evals.expected_output: Pushback with a specific alternative derived from the actual diff.
assertions: It reads the staged diff and proposes a specific subject
It explains what the vague subject costs a future blame or bisect reader
It defers to the user if they insist

evals.prompt: Write a commit message for this. Here is the tracker issue describing what we wanted to build.
evals.expected_output: A message describing the staged diff, not the issue.
assertions: It reads git diff --cached rather than writing from the issue text
If the diff differs from what the issue described, it describes the diff
It does not copy the issue description into the body
It does not use a closing keyword in the commit

evals.prompt: Add a body to this commit explaining what changed in each file.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to narrate files, with a body only if something non-obvious exists.
assertions: It does not produce a per-file narration
It writes a body only if the diff leaves something unexplained
If no such thing exists, it says the subject and diff are sufficient

evals.prompt: The fix looks trivial but the obvious version does not work because the lock is per-process. Commit it.
evals.expected_output: A body that records why the simpler fix fails.
assertions: A body is written
It states why the obvious implementation is insufficient
It does not narrate the code
It stays within a few short paragraphs

evals.prompt: Should I use feat: or fix: prefixes on these commits?
evals.expected_output: An answer grounded in whether anything in the repository consumes the prefix, established by checking rather than assumed.
assertions: It checks for release tooling, changelog generation, commitlint and a CI title check before answering
Where nothing consumes the prefix, the answer is no
The reason is that no tooling consumes the prefix, not that prefixes are bad
It names the condition under which the answer would change, such as adopting release tooling
It would conform if the repository did use them

evals.prompt: Commit this. Nothing has changed in the working tree, I already committed it earlier.
assertions: It checks the tree and finds no changes
It does not create an empty commit
It says plainly that there is nothing to commit

evals.prompt: These three commits on my branch are fine but the subjects are not uniform. Rewrite them to match.
evals.expected_output: Refusal to rewrite accurate history for cosmetic uniformity.
assertions: It does not rewrite the commits
It distinguishes cosmetic preference from a semantic problem
It routes any genuine rewriting need to rewriting-history

evals.prompt: I renamed the Session type to AuthSession across 180 files. Commit.
evals.expected_output: One commit, on the revert test.
assertions: It is one commit despite the file count
The reasoning references reverting one decision, not size
The subject names the rename and its object
